Downstream started. Comparing 4673346b (target branch) with de7fbea5 (this merge request). Run started by @AlphaTechini. Journeys first, then results.

## Journeys added

The scan found one changed function (the avatar colour helper) and no routes it maps to directly. Most pages go through one catch-all handler, so the journeys below are anonymous visitors opening pages that show avatars, using the pages listed in the repository's app notes. The demo user cannot sign in, so there are no sign-in, negative, repeated-create or second-user steps. The code I could read settles only the 200 statuses for these pages, so the gap remains.

### Existing parts the change reaches (compared old against new)

**Visitor opens the home page, explores projects and views the demo profile**
1. Open the home page.
2. Open the explore page.
3. Open the demo user's profile.
Why: calls the changed function, since these pages show avatars.

**Visitor opens the storefront repository and reads its commit history**
1. Open the repository home page.
2. Open the commit history.
Why: calls the changed function, since these pages show avatars.

**Visitor reads an issue and a merge request**
1. Open the issue list.
2. Open the first issue.
3. Open the merge request list.
4. Open the first merge request.
Why: calls the changed function, since issues and merge requests show author avatars.

### New feature (new build only)

None. The change adds no routes.

### Controls

**Visitor browses files and checks health**
1. Open the file tree.
2. Open a file.
3. Open the raw file.
4. Open the health check.
Why: control, pages that do not show avatars, to catch app-wide slowdowns.

*static analysis with go/ast, calls resolved by name, depth 2 from handlers and middleware, a function reached by more than half of all routes is ignored when looking for shared functions; misses dynamic registration, reflection, interface dispatch by other names, and cross-service calls*

**Not measured**

- DB time: not measured; the target exposes no database timing.

**Method.** Baseline run twice (B1, B2) and candidate once (C), in the order B1, C, B2, sequentially on one machine. Three runs give no confidence interval; treat verdicts near the thresholds as uncertain.

Gated metrics decide the verdict. For each, the worse baseline is the larger of B1 and B2, the noise band is the difference between them, and the allowed rise is the larger of a fraction of the worse baseline and an absolute figure. A metric is a regression when the candidate is above the worse baseline by more than the allowed rise and by more than the noise band, and improved by the opposite rule against the better baseline. When neither holds and the noise band is larger than the allowed rise, no verdict is given (withheld): a change of the allowed size could not be seen in this run. Smallest detectable is the larger of the allowed rise and the noise band. A step that passed on both baseline runs and failed on the candidate is a regression. One gated app metric clearly better and another clearly worse is reported as a trade-off.

Allowed rise by metric: CPU per completed journey 20% of the worse baseline; Bytes written per journey the larger of 1% of the worse baseline and an absolute 1024; Write syscalls per journey the larger of 4% of the worse baseline and an absolute 1; Open fds an absolute 1; Threads an absolute 2; Peak RSS the larger of 5% of the worse baseline and an absolute 10; Heap objects allocated per journey the larger of 10% of the worse baseline and an absolute 100; Heap bytes allocated per journey the larger of 5% of the worse baseline and an absolute 16384; GC cycles per pass an absolute 2; Goroutines an absolute 1.

Latency is advisory: a latency or total CPU figure is called slower when the candidate is worse than the worse baseline run by more than 2 times the noise band (the difference between B1 and B2), by at least 20%, and by at least 10 ms (latency) or 0.5 s (CPU). It never opens an issue.

#### Trend across merged merge requests

**Trend:** 1 of 6 metrics would have risen by 25% or more across the last merged merge requests if this one merges.

| Metric | Merged MRs counted | Their compounded change | This MR | Compounded if merged | Creep |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Heap bytes allocated per journey | 1 (!11) | -0.5% | -0.8% | -1.2% | no |
| Heap objects allocated per journey | 1 (!11) | -0.2% | -0.4% | -0.6% | no |
| CPU per journey | 1 (!11) | -2.3% | +206.6% | +199.5% | **yes** |
| Peak memory | 1 (!11) | -5.0% | -3.6% | -8.4% | no |
| Bytes written per journey | 1 (!11) | +0.0% | +0.2% | +0.2% | no |
| Write syscalls per journey | 1 (!11) | -0.1% | -0.4% | -0.6% | no |

Method: each merge request's change is its candidate against the worse of its two baselines, measured in one session, so changes from different sessions can be compounded even though absolute figures differ between sessions. A merged merge request is one whose recorded head is an ancestor of this run's base (squash merges are not traced). Window: the last 10 merged merge requests.

History is kept by the Downstream memory service on Google Cloud Run: https://downstream-memory-1083478229816.us-central1.run.app (numbers only, deleted after 30 days).
